text:
sara (support): FYI customer flagged a potentially exfiltrated artifact in their nightly backup. They say it's an exported KMS-wrapped key bundle and show an S3 path. Need immediate rotation guidance + audit export + retention answers.

mike (eng): Ack. Can you paste the exact S3 path & the filename they provided?

sara (support): s3://acme-backups/2026-03-15/exported_secrets.tar.gpg (they redacted most contents). They report two active API tokens after their in-app rotation.

jess (security): If they performed a user-level rotation but service tokens were long-lived, those will remain active. First short steps: 1) Create new scoped keys for affected apps. 2) Immediately revoke the old keys via admin API. 3) Collect evidence of any requests using the compromised tokens.

lina (infra): For evidence we can pull request logs + access logs. Ask customer for sample request IDs / timestamps. We can query: `GET /v1/internal/audit?user=acme&from=2026-03-14&to=2026-03-16` — will return usages, IPs, model ids.

mike (eng): Add to that: list active keys:```
GET /v1/internal/keys?org=acme
Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN
```That shows key ids + scopes + created_at. Revoke with `POST /v1/internal/keys/{key_id}/revoke`.

jess (security): Regarding wrapped export: if the file was wrapped with their KMS (customer-managed), the wrapping key's compromise is different. Ask whether the exported bundle contains plaintext API material or only KMS-wrapped blobs. If only wrapped blobs and their KMS is intact, rotate client-side secrets and rotate any KMS keys per their cloud provider guidance.

sara (support): Customer says the bundle included a `keys.json` file with a handful of base64-looking strings (they masked them). They are very concerned about retention & proof of deletion.

jess (security): We can provide audit exports showing our side's delete/revoke events and request logs. But we cannot attest for customer's backups — they must delete the S3 object. Provide them an action checklist: `1) rotate+issue new scoped keys 2) revoke old keys 3) run search/replace in their backup store + delete objects 4) export audit logs from us for the relevant time window`

lina (infra): To export logs: run the internal job `audit_log_export` in the console or use:```
POST /v1/internal/audit/export
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "org":"acme",
  "from":"2026-03-14T00:00:00Z",
  "to":"2026-03-16T23:59:59Z",
  "filters": {"event_types": ["request","key.rotate","key.revoke"]}
}
```We will return a signed URL with the export. Note retention: standard logs retained 90 days by default; can request extended retention for enterprise.

mike (eng): Also ask customer to search their app logs for `x-request-id` or for requests where `authorization: Bearer <token>` matches the compromised prefix (if they saved it). Even a prefix or first 6 chars helps correlate.

sara (support): Ops asked for proof they revoked keys. Can we provide revocation events & associated request ids?

jess (security): Yes — once we revoke via admin API we log an event `key.revoke` with actor, timestamp, and key_id. We'll include that in the audit export. If customer needs a signed attestation, we can generate a one-off statement (security@redwood) referencing the audit export and actions taken.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-2784 (severity: medium) — assigned to security.

mike (eng): I'll run the key listing + revoke for any keys the customer flags. Please provide the key ids or sample timestamps.

sara (support): I'll ask the customer for: object path + earliest/last seen + sample request ids + whether they rotated via console or API. Also ask if they used a customer-managed KMS or Redwood KMS.

jess (security): If they used Redwood-managed KMS and the bundle contains plaintext API keys, treat as full compromise: rotate all keys, reissue creds, check for unusual usage. If customer-managed KMS and wrapping key remains secure, scoped rotation + deletion of backups is acceptable.

sara (support): Understood. I'll collect artifacts and post back. For clarity, next steps we need to provide to customer: 1) exact revoke commands (we'll provide curl snippets) 2) audit export when ready 3) template language for their security team to confirm deletion of backups.

lina (infra): Also recommend rotating any downstream service accounts that had the key. Long-lived tokens should be phased to short-scoped tokens with shorter TTLs.

sara (support): Thanks team — will follow up in this thread once I have artifacts.

(End of thread)
